card.title: Coordination compounds — Werner's primary vs secondary valency

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The unit tours the blocks: p-block groups 15–18 (inert-pair effect, oxoacid trends, noble-gas aloofness), d-block (variable oxidation states, coloured paramagnetic ions, KMnO₄/K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidants, catalytic talent), f-block (lanthanoid contraction from poor 4f shielding). Coordination compounds crown it: Werner split valency into ionisable PRIMARY (oxidation state) and directional SECONDARY (coordination number) — [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ conducts 3 ions, [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ only 2, proving the split. IUPAC names ligands alphabetically; VBT/CFT explain colour and magnetism qualitatively; ionisation vs hydrate isomerism completes the set.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Werner: primary = oxidation state (ionisable) · secondary = coordination number (directional)  ·  [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ → 4 ions · [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ → 3 ions  ·  IUPAC: potassium hexacyanoferrate(II) = K₄[Fe(CN)₆]  ·  spin-only μ = √[n(n+2)] BM  ·  KMnO₄ (purple, +7 Mn) · K₂Cr₂O₇ (orange, +6 Cr)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Werner's conductivity test needs aqueous ionisation (non-electrolyte complexes give none). IUPAC ligand order is alphabetical ignoring multiplicative prefixes (di/tri). VBT hybridisation assignments (d²sp³ vs sp³d²) distinguish inner/outer orbital qualitatively. Lanthanoid contraction reasoning assumes steady 4f shielding failure.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Linkage isomerism (NO₂⁻ nitro vs nitrito) and ionisation isomerism ([Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br vs [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ — AgNO₃ precipitates only free Br⁻) are the favourite traps. KMnO₄ oxidises in acid (Mn²⁺, colourless), neutral (MnO₂) and alkaline (manganate green) — medium decides product. Prussian blue and chlorophyll-adjacent porphyrins show coordination everywhere.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: How many ions from [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂? Secondary valency (coordination sphere) holds 5NH₃ + 1Cl⁻ bound to Co; primary valency frees 2Cl⁻ → 1 complex cation + 2 anions = 3 ions (vs 4 from [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃). Conductance and AgCl precipitation counts confirm — Werner's theory verified by counting.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: VBT cannot explain spectra quantitatively or the spectrochemical series order from first principles (CFT does better, still qualitatively here). Werner predates orbitals — modern theory keeps his valencies, replaces his pictures. Lanthanoid/actinoid separations stay brutally hard (near-identical chemistry).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From conductivity + precipitation data: count free ions per formula → subtract from total ligands → bound set = coordination sphere; varying NH₃/Cl⁻ ratios across the CoCl₃·xNH₃ series (x = 6,5,4) yields 3,2,1 free Cl⁻ — primary valency constant (3+), secondary saturated at 6. CFT: d-orbitals split (t₂g/eg) in ligand fields; pairing vs Hund decides spin, colour follows Δ₀.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Ions on dissociation = 1 + free counter-ions (brackets stay intact). IUPAC: ligands alphabetical + metal + oxidation Roman + 'ate' for anionic complexes. Colour/magnetism: count d-electrons, split t₂g/eg, apply Hund. p-block trends: inert pair deepens down group 13–14.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: Werner's theory with ion-count proof; IUPAC names of two complexes; ionisation vs hydrate isomerism with AgNO₃ test; KMnO₄/K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidising uses; lanthanoid contraction reason.
